extraction.name: ScienceQA
extraction.description: ScienceQA is a new benchmark that consists of 21,208 multimodal multiple choice questions with diverse science topics and annotations of their answers with corresponding lectures and explanations. The dataset is collected from elementary and high school science curricula, covering three subjects: natural science, social science, and language science, across 26 topics, 127 categories, and 379 skills. Most questions are annotated with grounded lectures and detailed explanations to reveal the chain-of-thought reasoning process.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Tony Xia, Liang Qiu, Kai-Wei Chang, Song-Chun Zhu, Oyvind Tafjord, Peter Clark, Ashwin Kalyan
extraction.publisher: University of California, Los Angeles; Arizona State University; Allen Institute for AI
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Mishra, S., Xia, T., Qiu, L., Chang, K.-W., Zhu, S.-C., Tafjord, O., Clark, P., & Kalyan, A. (2022). Learn to Explain: Multimodal Reasoning via Thought Chains for Science Question Answering. 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022).
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions in the ScienceQA dataset are sourced from open resources managed by IXL Learning, an online learning platform curated by experts in the field of K-12 education. The dataset includes problems that align with California Common Core Content Standards. The original science problems were downloaded and then individual components (e.g. questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted based on heuristic rules. Invalid questions were manually removed, answer options were shuffled, and semi-automated scripts were used to reformat lectures and solutions. Incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Open resources managed by IXL Learning (https://www.ixl.com/), an online learning platform, with problems aligned to California Common Core Content Standards.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Invalid questions (questions with only one choice, questions containing faulty data, and duplicated questions) were manually removed. If there were multiple correct answers that applied, only one correct answer was kept. The answer options of each question were shuffled to ensure the choices do not follow any specific pattern. Semi-automated scripts were used to reformat the lectures and solutions so that special structures in the texts, such as tables and lists, are easily distinguishable from simple text passages.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Individual components (questions, hints, images, options, answers, lectures, and solutions) were extracted from the original science problems based on heuristic rules. For the baseline models, captions were extracted from a captioning model based on ViT and GPT-2 for images to serve as visual context. Newline separators (\n) in the text are replaced with \\n when encoding the inputs for language models.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (lectures and explanations) were sourced from the original science problems on IXL Learning. Incorrect annotations were further manually revised by experts. A data exploration tool was developed to review examples in the collected dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) was used for human performance evaluation and for evaluating generated explanations. A custom data exploration tool (https://scienceqa.github.io/explore.html) was developed for reviewing examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For human performance evaluation, each set of 15 questions (10 test + 5 exam examples) was assigned to 3 AMT workers. Only workers who correctly answered 4 out of 5 exam examples were qualified. For evaluating generated explanations, each batch of 10 samples was assigned to 3 workers to rate relevance, correctness, and completeness. Human scores for each explanation were determined by taking a majority vote.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 3 AMT workers per question for human performance evaluation; 3 workers per explanation for explanation quality evaluation
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: AMT workers who obtained a high school or higher degree and passed qualification examples were qualified for the human performance study.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ViT + GPT-2 based captioning model (nlpconnect/vit-gpt2-image-captioning) for generating image captions as visual context.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and code are available at https://scienceqa.github.io. The dataset is available for non-commercial research purposes only and the copyright belongs to the original authors.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset does not contain any user usage data or personally sensitive information such as gender and race. After careful examination, no improper content such as pornographic information, racial remarks, or harmful social bias was found.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: ScienceQA provides a useful benchmark for multi-modal learning, multi-hop reasoning, and general artificial intelligence. It will contribute to the development of K-12 education applications such as tutoring systems. The designed methods with the chain of thought investigate the ability of large language models to mimic the human mind process when reasoning about challenging tasks. The authors adhere to the goal of AI for the common good, and any antisocial data points will be removed from the dataset based on feedback.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: GPT-3 via chain-of-thought prompting still fails to answer a wide range of challenging questions. Failure cases include: (a) the model fails to understand the multimodal inputs and lacks domain-specific knowledge to arrive at the correct answer; (b) the model generates the wrong chain of thought with irrelevant, incorrect, or incomplete information. Extracted image captions lack fine-grained semantics and usually do not work well for diagrams. There exist challenges for large language models to reason about questions that require them to understand complex and uncommon domain knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is split into training (12,726 examples), validation (4,241 examples), and test (4,241 examples) splits with a ratio of 60:20:20. Use cases include training, validation, and testing for multimodal question answering, multi-hop reasoning, chain-of-thought generation, few-shot learning, and fine-tuning of language models. The dataset is for non-commercial research purposes only.
